newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 65,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 65,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award 60,000 to 65,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
There was no tender last week but at the last tender, on March 19, the EU awarded 43,500 tonnes.
This week's maximum restitution level was estimated at 44.329 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kilos of sugar after the 44.180 Ecus awarded on March 19.
This prediction is on the assumption that the EU will use the Paris August price in its calculations, one trader said. There is a chance May could be used, he said.
Licences are currently valid until the end of September.

The March 19 award brought the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.680 million tonnes. It compares with a tonnage of 1.722 million tonnes by March 20 1996. --Christopher Lyddon, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7928
